en: The Sūtra on the Duration of the Dharma as Recorded by the Buddha at the Time of His Parinirvāṇa, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavat was staying in the city of Kuśinagara, at the birthplace of the Mallas.

At the Śāla grove of twin trees, he was accompanied by immeasurable and incalculable numbers of śrāvakas and bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as well as devas, humans, asuras, and others, with the entire great assembly surrounding him in front and behind.
At that time, as the Bhagavān was approaching parinirvāṇa, out of compassion for sentient beings, he addressed Ānanda with a voice of loving-kindness and gentleness, saying:
"I shall now soon enter parinirvāṇa; I have relinquished all conditioned phenomena without exception, and all Buddha-activities have been brought to ultimate completion."

I have already proclaimed the Dharma that is free from the cave-dwelling of existence, the sublime nectar-like Dharma, the Dharma of supreme sovereignty, and the Dharma of ultimate peace and bliss. This Dharma is profound and subtle, difficult to understand and difficult to know; it is beyond discursive thought and transcends the sphere of conceptualization, to be personally realized within by the great noble ones.

I have further turned the unsurpassed Wheel of Dharma three times; this wheel is majestic and powerful, endowed with twelve characteristics, such that no other śramaṇas, brahmins, devas, māras, or Brahmās are able to turn it in accordance with reality.
I have already blown the great Dharma conch and struck the great Dharma drum for all devas and humans, awakening them from the sleep of ignorance throughout the long night.
I have already erected the great Dharma banner and lit the great Dharma torch for all devas and humans, universally illuminating everything to eliminate all darkness.
I have already constructed for all sentient beings the great bridge of Dharma and the great ship of Dharma, to ferry across all those drowning in the violent currents.
I have already poured forth the great stream of Dharma and brought down the great rain of Dharma, causing all that is withered and parched to be thoroughly moistened and saturated.

I have already revealed the correct path to liberation and led those throughout the world who had lost their way; all sentient beings whom I was to deliver have now been delivered, and for all those not yet delivered, I have likewise established the causes and conditions for their deliverance.
I have already subdued all non-Buddhists;
I have already crushed all heterodox doctrines;
I have already overturned the palaces of all Māras.

I have already destroyed all the armies of Māra, uttered the true lion’s roar, and performed the great work of a Buddha; I have fulfilled the original vows of a Great Being, protected the Eye of the Dharma so that it remains without flaw or deficiency, transformed the śrāvakas, and bestowed the prediction of enlightenment upon the bodhisattvas. As the unsurpassed Buddha-eye for future ages, I shall illuminate the world, forever and without interruption.
Ānanda! You all should diligently protect and uphold such unsurpassed true Dharma so that it does not perish or disappear. Ānanda!
"I now have nothing further to do; only the Great Nirvāṇa is my destination.
At that time, having heard the Buddha’s words, Ānanda was overcome with grief and longing. After a long silence, he spoke:

"I do not yet know, O Tathāgata, for how long after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa will the unsurpassed True Dharma—attained through the diligent toil of three incalculable eons for the sake of all sentient beings—remain in the world to benefit devas, humans, asuras, and others, before it gradually vanishes?"
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed Ānanda with a compassionate voice, saying:
"The transformative traces of all Buddhas are invariably like this; do not grieve or lament any longer."
After my parinirvāṇa, this unsurpassed True Dharma shall remain in the world for a thousand years, benefiting devas, humans, asuras, and others; after that time, it will gradually disappear.

“Ānanda! You should know that one hundred years after my parinirvāṇa, the sublime Dharma within my holy teaching will remain firm. My disciples will be wise and learned, possessing fearless eloquence capable of subduing heterodox arguments and endowed with great supernormal powers; they will bring much benefit to sentient beings.

For this reason, devas and nāgas will rejoice and diligently provide protection, and likewise kings, ministers, elders, and householders will recognize the field of merit, conceiving deep pure faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, and will offer them worship, respect, honor, and praise.”

At the end of one hundred years, there will appear in the world a great king named Aśoka, who, possessing great power, shall rule over Jambudvīpa. He will construct eighty-four thousand stūpas, lofty, vast, and magnificently adorned, to enshrine the relics of my body that I have left behind, causing immeasurable multitudes to see and hear them with joy, so that they all establish the karma for rebirth in the heavens and liberation.

“Two hundred years after my parinirvāṇa, my holy teaching will be tranquil and firm; my disciples will be wise and learned, like Teachers of Gods and Humans, possessing great majesty and virtue, and bringing benefit to many.

For this reason, devas and nāgas will rejoice and constantly provide protection, and likewise kings, ministers, elders, and householders will recognize the field of merit, develop deep pure faith in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and offer them worship, respect, honor, and praise.”

“Three hundred years after my parinirvāṇa, the correct practice within my holy teaching will remain firm. My disciples who have attained liberation through wisdom, those liberated both ways, body-witnesses, and those who have reached the stage of vision—countless hundreds of thousands of such as these—will exist because many people will attain the fruits of the noble path. Consequently, devas and nāgas will rejoice and constantly provide protection; likewise, kings, ministers, elders, and householders, recognizing the field of merit well, will develop deep pure faith in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, making offerings, paying homage, honoring, and praising them.”
“Four hundred years after my parinirvāṇa, my holy teaching will be free from rigidity; my disciples will delight in dwelling in seclusion and diligently cultivate tranquil concentration.

For this reason, devas and nāgas will rejoice and constantly follow to protect them, as will kings, ministers, elders, and householders. Being well-acquainted with the field of merit, they will conceive deep, pure faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising them.”

"In the fifth century after my parinirvāṇa, the Dharma and its meaning shall remain firm within my holy teaching; my disciples will love and delight in the True Dharma, diligently practicing study and engaging in debate and discernment.

Because of this, devas and nāgas will rejoice and constantly provide diligent protection, and likewise kings, ministers, elders, and householders will recognize the field of merit, conceiving deep pure faith in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, making offerings, showing reverence, honoring, and praising them."

"Six hundred years after my parinirvāṇa, the Dharma-teaching within my holy dispensation shall remain firm. My disciples will for the most part apply themselves diligently to the study and recitation of the teachings, their minds free from weariness, and they will be able to bring great benefit to immeasurable sentient beings.

For this reason, devas and nāgas will rejoice and exert themselves in providing protection; likewise, kings, ministers, elders, and householders will recognize the field of merit, develop deep pure faith in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and offer them offerings, respect, honor, and praise, yet they will harbor many doubts regarding the underlying meaning."

“Seven hundred years after my parinirvāṇa, within my holy teaching, the pursuit of gain and offerings will become firm; devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, and others will offer worship, respect, honor, and praise to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha. My disciples will for the most part become attached to gain, honor, and reputation, and will not diligently cultivate the higher trainings in virtue, concentration, and wisdom.”

"Eight hundred years after my parinirvāṇa, strife and contention will become entrenched within my holy teaching. My disciples will for the most part harbor mutual jealousy; they will conspire with wicked people, spreading dust-like slander and defamation. They will hold those who maintain the precepts in contempt and look down upon those of great learning. They will not mind the 'Six Points of Concord' but will focus their thoughts on discord. Seeing what is unskillful, they will show no respect for teachers and elders, dwelling in a state of lack of right comprehension. Deceitful and crooked, their speech will be as coarse and wild as that of a candāla. They will rely upon kings, ministers, and householders, using expedient means to waste and squander the wealth and property of the Triple Gem, forming evil factions to suppress and crush virtuous people."

"Nine hundred years after my parinirvāṇa, the activities within my holy teaching will become firm; many of my disciples will engage in worldly occupations such as agriculture and commerce, and they will sustain themselves by serving as messengers, becoming lax and transgressing the training rules (śikṣāpada) established by the Tathāgatas."

"In the tenth century after my parinirvāṇa, within my holy teaching, frivolous proliferation (*prapañca*) will become firm. My disciples will for the most part diligently study various forms of frivolous proliferation, abandoning the supramundane, authentic teachings of the Buddhas—namely, the discourses (*sūtra*), verses (*geya*), prophecies (*vyākaraṇa*), stanzas (*gāthā*), utterances (*udāna*), causal origins (*nidāna*), parables (*avadāna*), past events (*itivṛttaka*), birth stories (*jātaka*), extensive teachings (*vaipulya*), marvelous events (*adbhutadharma*), and expositions (*upadeśa*)—and instead will zealously practice and recite mundane frivolous proliferations, namely: treatises on kings, treatises on thieves, treatises on war, treatises on food, treatises on drink, treatises on clothing, treatises on vehicles, treatises on the self, treatises on women, treatises on men, treatises on various lands, treatises on rivers and oceans, and treatises on non-Buddhist paths."
Because they delight in these various forms of conceptual proliferation, they cause śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and others to disparage and fall away from my noble teaching.

Within my True Dharma and Vinaya, there shall be such evil bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs who do not properly cultivate bodily discipline, mental concentration, or wisdom; they will contend with one another in anger, plotting to destroy and slander each other, and becoming deeply attached to various fine robes, alms bowls, dwellings, and bedding. Because they associate and assemble with such evil companions, even if they have guarded the pure precepts for many years, they will violate them all in a single moment; and even if they have accumulated roots of virtue for many years, they will lose them all through their excessive grief and resentment.

For these reasons, the assemblies of devas, nāgas, and others will feel sorrow and distress, and they will abandon their protective guardianship. Kings, ministers, elders, and householders will no longer give rise to pure faith toward the Triple Gem; instead, they will slander and disparage it. By these causes and conditions, the True Dharma will be extinguished.
"From this time forward, as the evil deeds of the bhikṣus become increasingly deep, kings, ministers, elders, and householders will show less and less respect.

Yet, because the remaining power of the Triple Gem has not yet entirely perished, at that time there will again be bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs who have few desires and are content, who guard the prohibitive precepts, practice meditative concentration, delight in extensive learning, and uphold the Tathāgata’s teachings of the Tripiṭaka; they will extensively analyze and expound them for the fourfold assembly, benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to immeasurable sentient beings.

Furthermore, there will be kings, ministers, elders, and householders who cherish the True Dharma, making offerings, showing respect, honoring, and praising the Triple Gem, protecting and establishing it without regard for their own interests."

You should know that all these are inconceivable bodhisattvas who, by the power of their original vows, have appeared at this time to uphold the unsurpassed true Dharma of the Tathāgata and to bring great benefit to all sentient beings.

At that time, Ānanda, the śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, non-humans, and the entire great assembly, having heard the Bhagavān’s prophetic declaration regarding the duration of the future persistence of the Dharma and the diverse karmic activities of the bhikṣus, were all moved to increased lamentation; they accepted it with faith and respectfully put it into practice.
The Sūtra on the Duration of the Dharma as Recorded by the Buddha at the Time of His Parinirvāṇa.
